explanation: Fires retrospectively at the line-break (newline) token that ends a line whose leading indentation is about 6-11 spaces (peak at 8-10 spaces): a deep-indent line ending in block-structured text, strongest when that line ends with an opening delimiter ('(', '[', '{', '=') and weakest when it ends with a closer (')', ';'), and silent when the same words are unindented (0-4 spaces) or when the long space run is mid-line rather than at the line start. Its peaks do not depend on what follows the line break (next-line indentation 8 vs 12 vs 16 leaves the peak unchanged), which is why it is retrospective; the pole also fires diffusely at 1-2.5 on ordinary function words and periods inside some web/news and non-English documents, a register-like leftover that this line-break rule does not cover.
